question_text: A concave mirror has focal length 20 cm. An object is placed 30 cm in front of it. The image distance is:
explanation: With u = −30 and f = −20, 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/20 + 1/30 = −1/60, so v = −60 cm: a real image 60 cm in front of the mirror.
subject: Physics

question_text: A convex mirror has focal length 15 cm. An object is placed 15 cm in front of it. The image is:

options.A: real, 30 cm in front of the mirror
options.B: real, 15 cm in front of the mirror
options.D: virtual, 7.5 cm in front of the mirror

explanation: With u = −15 and f = +15, 1/v = 1/15 + 1/15 = 2/15, so v = +7.5 cm: a virtual image behind the mirror.
subject: Physics

question_text: Which statements about a concave mirror are correct?

options.A: It can form a real image
options.B: It forms a virtual, enlarged image when the object is between the pole and the focus
options.C: It always forms a diminished image
options.D: Its focal length is half its radius of curvature

explanation: A concave mirror can form real or virtual images, with f = R/2. It forms enlarged images for objects between f and 2f, so C is false.
subject: Physics

question_text: Which statements about total internal reflection are correct?

options.A: It can occur only when light travels from a denser to a rarer medium
options.B: It requires the angle of incidence to exceed the critical angle
options.C: It is used in optical fibres
options.D: It can occur when light travels from air into glass

explanation: TIR needs a denser-to-rarer path and an angle of incidence above the critical angle. Light going from air into glass cannot undergo TIR.
subject: Physics
